findings.title: Date-override days skip the busy-time check, enabling double bookings
findings.body: In checkIfIsAvailable, when any date override matches the slot's day, `dateOverrideExist` is set to true and, if the slot falls inside the override window (so the `find` callback never returns true), the function hits `if (dateOverrideExist) { return true; }` — returning 'available' before the `busy.every(...)` check at the bottom ever runs. This means that on any day where a host has a date override, that host's existing bookings and calendar busy times are completely ignored. A fixed host (or a regular solo event user, since they are also isFixed) with a date override who already has a booking/meeting inside the override window will be shown as bookable, producing double bookings — the exact problem this PR claims to fix ('prevents round-robin events being booked where the fixed hosts are unavailable'). The busy check must still run when a date override exists; only the working-hours check should be bypassed.

findings.title: `end` in the working-hours check is a copy-paste of `start`
findings.body: In the new working-hours block of checkIfIsAvailable: `const start = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute(); const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();` — `end` should be computed from `slotEndTime` (i.e. slotStartTime + eventLength). As written, end === start, so the check `end > workingHour.endTime` only verifies that the slot *starts* before the working-hours end. A slot that starts inside the fixed host's working hours but finishes after their end time (e.g. host available 09:00–12:00, a 60-minute slot at 11:30–12:30 contributed by another round-robin host's wider availability) passes the check and is bookable, letting invitees book time the fixed host is not available.

findings.title: dayjs objects compared with `===` — always false
findings.body: `if (dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes') === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, 'minutes'))` compares two distinct dayjs object instances by reference, which is always false (`.isSame()` was presumably intended). This branch exists to detect a blocked-day override (start === end, i.e. 'unavailable the whole day'). Because it never fires, a blocked day is only rejected incidentally via the before/after checks, and a slot starting exactly at the block's start instant satisfies none of them: the callback returns undefined, `dateOverrideExist` is already true, and the function returns `true` (available) — leaking a bookable slot on a day the host explicitly marked unavailable.

findings.title: Multiple same-day date-override windows veto each other
findings.body: The `dateOverrides.find(...)` logic treats 'slot is outside this one override window' as grounds to return false (unavailable), but a user can have several override windows on the same date (cal.com's UI allows adding multiple time ranges to one date override, stored as separate rows). For a slot that falls inside window B, window A's callback hits `slotStartTime.isAfter(date.end)` (or `slotEndTime.isBefore(date.start)`) and returns true, so the slot is marked unavailable even though it is within window B — and vice versa. Net effect: on a day with two or more override windows, every window is rejected by the other and the host shows no availability at all. The find should only return a 'reject' verdict after confirming the slot is outside *all* same-day windows for that user.

findings.title: Override decoding depends on the server running in UTC
findings.body: The new code decodes the override's wall-clock-encoded Date back to a real instant with `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes')` and compares it against `slotStartTime`/`slotEndTime`, which are explicitly UTC (`time.utc()`). `dayjs(date.start)` parses the Date in the process's local timezone, so the decode math (wall time − organizer offset = real UTC instant) only holds when the Node process runs with TZ=UTC. On any non-UTC runtime (dev machines, some CI/self-hosted setups) the override window and day-matching comparisons are shifted by the server offset, making fixed-host override filtering silently wrong. Use `dayjs.utc(date.start)` for these comparisons, as the parallel code in packages/lib/slots.ts already does with `.utc()`.

findings.title: Offset-shifted override times discard the day component
findings.body: The invitee-timezone conversion computes `startTime`/`endTime` as `dayjs(override.start).utc().add(offset, 'minute').hour() * 60 + ...minute()`. Taking `.hour()/.minute()` after the offset shift drops any day rollover: when the invitee/organizer offset difference pushes the override across midnight (e.g. organizer Asia/Kolkata override 01:00–02:00 = 19:30–20:30 the previous UTC day, viewed by a UTC invitee: offset = −330 min lands on the previous day, but hour() yields 1170 minutes), the slot is materialized at 19:30 on the *current* invitee day instead of the correct adjacent day. Since the activeOverrides filter keys on the unshifted date, cross-midnight overrides are placed on the wrong day — precisely the timezone-adjustment scenario this PR is fixing. The shifted value should be carried as a full timestamp (or the day delta applied to startOfInviteeDay), not reduced to minutes-since-midnight.

findings.title: override.timeZone is optional in the type but required by the conversion
findings.body: `dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone).utcOffset()` assumes `override.timeZone` is set, but the `TimeRange` type declares `timeZone?: string` as optional and getSlots is a shared library function — nothing at the type level guarantees every caller supplies it (the slots router happens to add it in this PR). With `timeZone` undefined, dayjs's tz plugin falls back to the host system's timezone when computing `organizerUtcOffset`, so the offset correction is silently computed against the server timezone and override slots are shifted by a wrong amount. Either make the field required for date overrides passed to getSlots or guard/default it here.

findings.title: No test coverage for the round-robin fixed-host date-override fix
findings.body: The PR's primary purpose is making date overrides (and working hours) of *fixed hosts* apply to round-robin events via the new logic in checkIfIsAvailable, and the PR description lists a round-robin fixed-host scenario as the main test plan. However, the only test added exercises a single-user personal event with a different invitee timezone. None of the new checkIfIsAvailable behavior — fixed host availability gating, override-window filtering per host, interaction with busy times — is covered, which is how the regression where busy checks are skipped on override days (and the multi-window veto issue) went unnoticed. A round-robin scenario with one fixed host having a date override should be added, including a case where the fixed host is busy inside the override window.
